title: Kixie Review (2026)
intro: Kixie is an AI-powered sales dialer and business phone platform built to sit inside a CRM: click-to-call, PowerDialer, SMS, call recording, and conversation intelligence. This review scores it on SoftwareGlimpse's sales intelligence methodology — contact data, prospecting, enrichment, email outreach, CRM sync, usability, reporting, and value — which is the fairest way to show where a calling layer helps a prospecting stack and where it simply does not participate.
summary: Kixie is a strong calling and CRM-activity layer that contributes almost nothing to prospect sourcing. CRM sync and conversation reporting score high; contact data and email outreach score low by design. Treat it as a complement to a data vendor, not a replacement. Scores come from first-party kixie.com research, not hands-on lab testing.
verdict: Kixie is the calling execution layer beneath a sales intelligence stack rather than a member of it. Bi-directional CRM sync, PowerDialer throughput, and conversation intelligence are genuinely strong, but Kixie sources no contacts and sends no email sequences, so it always needs a data provider and usually an email tool alongside it. Seat prices are not published on the official pricing page, so total cost requires a quote covering seats plus the add-ons you actually need. This review is based on first-party kixie.com documentation — not hands-on product testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Kixie has no B2B contact database. Contact management is supported in the sense that it holds and dials records synced from a CRM, but every number it calls originates somewhere else — this is an execution layer, not a data source.

Lead management is documented as limited and there is no prospect search, so Kixie cannot find prospects; what it does exceptionally well is work a list — multi-line PowerDialer throughput is a genuine prospecting-velocity advantage once the list exists.

Kixie enriches records behaviourally rather than firmographically: call outcomes, dispositions, recordings, and transcripts write back to the CRM contact. Useful data, but it adds no third-party firmographic or contact-detail enrichment.

Email sequencing is not documented as a capability in this research pass. Kixie's multichannel story is phone plus SMS, so automated SMS follow-up covers part of the sequencing job while email is left entirely to another tool.

Bi-directional CRM integration is the product's defining feature, with HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, and Zapier documented on the homepage and workflow automation supported — calls, SMS, recordings, and dispositions log against the right record without rep effort.

Click-to-call from inside the CRM, three clearly named plans mapped to dialing intensity, and a no-credit-card trial make this easy to adopt; a rep's daily surface is a dialer bar, not a new application to learn.

Reporting is documented as supported and AI assistance is supported, covering call analytics, connect rates, and AI Insights or Conversation Intelligence — genuinely strong for a communications layer and better than most data vendors manage.

All three plans are contact-sales with no published dollar amounts, and premium add-ons stack on top, so value cannot be assessed without a quote. The 7-day no-credit-card trial partly offsets this by allowing evaluation before the pricing conversation.

Contact-center-style inbound teams needing routing alongside outbound dialing

whoShouldChoose: Calling-first outbound teams already running a CRM as their system of record, who want dial throughput, automatic activity logging, and conversation intelligence — and who already have a separate source for prospect data.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Teams that need prospect sourcing should pair Kixie with Lusha or BookYourData rather than substituting one for the other; buyers wanting dialing, data, and email sequencing in one subscription should compare Apollo or Reply; and shoppers who need published pricing to shortlist will find Kixie's quote-gated plans frustrating.

faq.question: How much does Kixie cost?
faq.answer: Kixie prices per seat in USD across Professional, Single-Line PowerDialer, and Multi-Line PowerDialer, but all three are contact-sales with no dollar amounts published on the official pricing page. There is no free plan; a 7-day trial with no credit card lets you evaluate first. Premium add-ons are priced separately, so ask for a quote covering seats plus add-ons.

faq.question: Does Kixie provide B2B contact data?
faq.answer: No. Kixie is a dialer and business phone platform, not a data provider. Every number it calls comes from your CRM or a separate data vendor such as Lusha, Apollo, or BookYourData. Budget for a data source alongside it rather than expecting Kixie to replace one.

faq.question: Can Kixie run email sequences?
faq.answer: No. Email sequencing is not a documented capability. Kixie's multichannel story is phone plus SMS, including automated SMS follow-up triggered by call outcomes, but email outreach needs a separate tool such as Reply or Apollo.

faq.question: Which CRMs does Kixie integrate with?
faq.answer: The homepage documents HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, and Zapier with bi-directional integration called out across plans. Calls, SMS, recordings, and dispositions log back against the CRM record automatically, which is the strongest column on Kixie's sales intelligence scorecard.

faq.question: What is the difference between the PowerDialer plans?
faq.answer: Professional covers business phone and click-to-call, Single-Line PowerDialer adds sequential automated dialing, and Multi-Line PowerDialer dials up to four lines simultaneously for maximum connect throughput. The right rung depends on daily dial volume rather than team size.

faq.question: Is this a hands-on SoftwareGlimpse lab review?
faq.answer: No. This review is approved on the basis of first-party kixie.com research covering the homepage and pricing page. SoftwareGlimpse has not recorded hands-on product testing for Kixie in this assessment, and scores carry medium confidence accordingly.

sections.heading: What Kixie is
sections.body: Kixie is an AI-powered sales dialer and business phone platform for CRM-connected outbound calling, SMS, and coaching. The vendor positions it as a communications platform for revenue teams covering power dialing, contact center, SMS, and conversation intelligence. In sales intelligence terms it is an execution layer: it makes the contacting fast and the logging automatic, but it never tells you who to contact.

sections.heading: Pricing and plans
sections.body: Three per-seat plans in USD — Professional, Single-Line PowerDialer, and Multi-Line PowerDialer — all quote-gated with no published dollar amounts. There is no free plan, though a 7-day trial without a credit card allows real evaluation before the sales conversation. Premium add-ons including ConnectionBoost, Conversation Intelligence, AI Human Detection, and DNC scrubbing price separately, so the seat rate alone will understate total cost.

sections.heading: CRM sync and activity capture
sections.body: This is Kixie's strongest sales intelligence column. Bi-directional integration with HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, and Zapier means click-to-call works from inside the CRM and every call, SMS, recording, and disposition writes back to the right record without rep effort. Workflow automation triggers follow-up actions from call outcomes. For managers, the payoff is that activity data is complete rather than dependent on reps remembering to log calls.

sections.heading: Dial throughput and where the data comes from
sections.body: The PowerDialer ladder scales from click-to-call up to four simultaneous lines, and add-ons like ConnectionBoost target connect rates directly. That throughput is a real prospecting-velocity advantage — but only once a list exists. Lead management is documented as limited and there is no prospect search, so Kixie always needs a data source upstream: your CRM, or a provider such as Lusha, Apollo, or BookYourData.

sections.heading: Reporting and conversation intelligence
sections.body: Reporting is documented as supported and AI assistance is supported, covering call analytics, connect rates, and AI Insights or Conversation Intelligence over recordings and transcripts. This is stronger than most data vendors manage and is the second reason Kixie earns its place beside a prospecting stack: it turns calls into coachable, measurable data rather than untracked activity. AI recommendations are documented as limited, so treat prioritization as lighter than the analytics layer.

sections.heading: Who it's for
sections.body: Best for calling-first outbound teams on a mainstream CRM who want dial throughput, automatic activity capture, and conversation intelligence. Weak fit if you are shopping for prospect data, if your motion is email-first, or if you need published pricing to shortlist. The correct mental model is complement, not substitute: Kixie plus a data provider plus a CRM, or Apollo and Reply if you want fewer vendors.

productExperience.summary: The daily loop lives inside the CRM: a rep opens a contact list synced from HubSpot or Salesforce, launches PowerDialer, works connects with local presence and voicemail drop, triggers SMS follow-up from call outcomes, and managers review recordings and Conversation Intelligence afterwards.

workflowSteps.title: Sync the call list
workflowSteps.description: Pull contacts from HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, or Pipedrive via bi-directional integration — Kixie never sources the list itself.

workflowSteps.title: Run PowerDialer
workflowSteps.description: Dial sequentially or across up to four simultaneous lines depending on plan, with connect-rate add-ons layered on.

workflowSteps.title: Trigger SMS follow-up
workflowSteps.description: Fire templated SMS and voicemail drops automatically from call dispositions rather than manually after each attempt.

workflowSteps.title: Auto-log to CRM
workflowSteps.description: Calls, texts, recordings, and dispositions write back to the CRM record without rep data entry.

workflowSteps.title: Coach on conversations
workflowSteps.description: Managers use live whisper and barge during calls, then review AI Insights and Conversation Intelligence over recordings.

productExperience.evidenceNote: Workflow reconstructed from first-party kixie.com homepage and pricing pages — not from SoftwareGlimpse hands-on testing.

detailedSections.title: Contact data
detailedSections.summary: There is no database. Kixie holds and dials records that originate somewhere else entirely.
body: Contact management is documented as supported, but that means Kixie stores, organizes, and dials contacts synced from a CRM — not that it can supply new ones. There is no prospect index, no reveal action, and no credits, because there is nothing to reveal.

This is the single most important thing for a buyer to understand before shortlisting. A team evaluating Kixie against Lusha or BookYourData is comparing products that do not overlap: one supplies phone numbers, the other dials them. The realistic stack is both.
strengths: Holds and organizes CRM-synced contacts cleanly for dialing
Local presence dialing improves connect rates on existing numbers
weaknesses: No B2B contact database or prospect index
Cannot supply new phone numbers or email addresses
Always requires a separate data vendor or CRM as the source

detailedSections.title: Prospecting
detailedSections.summary: Cannot find prospects, but works a list faster than almost anything else in the category.
body: Lead management is documented as limited and there is no prospect search, so the discovery half of prospecting is entirely absent. Judged on sourcing alone, this would score near the floor.

The reason it scores 6 is throughput. Multi-Line PowerDialer runs up to four simultaneous lines, and connect-rate add-ons target the specific failure mode of outbound calling — reaching nobody. For teams whose prospecting constraint is dials-per-hour rather than list quality, that is a genuine and underrated advantage.
strengths: Multi-line dialing up to four simultaneous lines for maximum throughput
Connect-rate add-ons address the real bottleneck in outbound calling
Local presence and voicemail drop reduce time lost per attempt
weaknesses: No prospect search or discovery capability at all
List quality is entirely inherited from upstream systems

detailedSections.title: Data enrichment
detailedSections.summary: Enriches behaviour, not firmographics — call outcomes and transcripts, never job titles or company data.
body: Every call produces data that flows back to the CRM record: disposition, duration, recording, transcript, and any automated follow-up triggered by workflow automation. That is real enrichment, and it is the kind a data vendor cannot provide.

It is not, however, what the sales intelligence category usually means by enrichment. There is no third-party append of firmographics, technographics, or missing contact details, so a stale CRM stays stale on every dimension except call history. Score it as a useful complement to a data-enrichment layer rather than a substitute.
strengths: Call outcomes, recordings, and transcripts append to the CRM record automatically
Workflow automation turns dispositions into downstream actions
Behavioural data no third-party provider can supply
weaknesses: No firmographic, technographic, or contact-detail append
Does not correct or refresh stale CRM fields

detailedSections.title: Email outreach
detailedSections.summary: No email sequencing. SMS automation covers part of the follow-up job; email is somebody else's product.
body: Email sequencing is documented as unknown in this research pass, and the product positioning gives no reason to expect otherwise — Kixie is phone and SMS first, with meeting scheduling also undocumented.

The partial credit here is SMS. Templated texts and voicemail drops fire automatically from call dispositions, which does cover the mechanical follow-up job that email sequences usually handle, just in a different channel. For calling-first teams that is often sufficient; for anyone running a mixed-channel motion, a separate sequencer is mandatory.
strengths: Automated SMS follow-up triggered by call dispositions
Voicemail drop removes repeated manual message recording
weaknesses: No documented email sequencing or mailbox integration
Meeting scheduling also undocumented in this research pass
Mixed-channel teams need a second outreach tool

detailedSections.title: CRM sync
detailedSections.summary: The best column on the scorecard — bi-directional integration is the whole architectural premise.
body: Kixie is built to live inside a CRM rather than beside one. HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, and Zapier are documented on the homepage with bi-directional integration called out across plans, and workflow automation is a supported capability.

The practical value is data completeness. Because click-to-call originates from the CRM record, activity logging is not something reps have to remember — calls, texts, recordings, and dispositions land automatically. Anyone who has audited a CRM where half the calls were never logged will recognize how much that is worth for forecasting and coaching alike.
strengths: Bi-directional integration with HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, Pipedrive, and Zapier
Activity logging is automatic rather than rep-dependent
Workflow automation triggers CRM actions from call outcomes
Click-to-call originates from inside the CRM record
weaknesses: Depth of field mapping varies by connector and plan

detailedSections.title: Ease of use
detailedSections.summary: Reps live in a dialer bar inside a tool they already use — adoption friction is close to zero.
body: The daily surface for a rep is click-to-call inside the CRM, not a new application to learn, which removes the single biggest cause of failed sales-tool rollouts. The three plan names map transparently onto dialing intensity.

The complexity that does exist is administrative rather than user-facing: number provisioning, carrier reputation, DNC compliance, and add-on configuration all need an owner. That is telephony overhead rather than product design, but it should be staffed rather than assumed away.
strengths: Click-to-call inside the existing CRM means minimal rep retraining
Plan names map directly onto dialing intensity
7-day trial with no credit card enables real evaluation
weaknesses: Number health, carrier reputation, and DNC compliance need an admin owner

detailedSections.title: Reporting
detailedSections.summary: Call analytics plus conversation intelligence — better reporting than most data vendors in the category offer.
body: Reporting is documented as supported and AI assistance is supported, covering connect rates, call volume, rep activity, and AI Insights or Conversation Intelligence over recordings and transcripts.

The distinction worth drawing is between activity reporting and conversation reporting. Most tools stop at the former; Kixie's transcript-level analysis lets managers see what was actually said, which is the difference between knowing a rep made 60 dials and knowing why 55 of them went nowhere. AI recommendations are documented as limited, so the system describes better than it prescribes.
strengths: Connect rate, volume, and rep activity analytics as standard
Conversation Intelligence over recordings and transcripts
Live whisper and barge support in-the-moment coaching
weaknesses: Conversation Intelligence is a paid add-on rather than standard

detailedSections.title: Value for money
detailedSections.summary: Unassessable without a quote — no published seat prices, and add-ons stack on top.
body: All three plans are contact-sales with no dollar amounts on the official pricing page, and there is no free plan. That alone caps this score: value is a ratio, and one side of it is missing.

The add-on structure compounds the problem. ConnectionBoost, Conversation Intelligence, AI Human Detection, and DNC scrubbing are the features most buyers actually want, and they price separately, so a quoted seat rate can understate real cost substantially. The 7-day no-credit-card trial is the mitigation — evaluate the product properly before you have the pricing conversation, then quote seats plus add-ons together.
strengths: 7-day trial without a credit card allows evaluation before commitment
Unlimited US and Canada minutes positioning simplifies usage forecasting
weaknesses: No published seat prices on any of the three plans
Premium add-ons price separately and stack on the seat rate
No free plan for open-ended evaluation

limitations.title: Not a data source
limitations.explanation: Kixie has no contact database. Every number it dials originates in your CRM or a separate data vendor, so it can never be the whole answer to a prospecting problem.
limitations.whoItAffects: Teams whose constraint is finding prospects rather than reaching them

limitations.title: No email sequencing
limitations.explanation: Email sequencing is not documented, so mixed-channel outbound requires a second tool. SMS automation covers follow-up within the phone channel only.
limitations.whoItAffects: Teams running email-first or mixed-channel outbound motions

limitations.title: Quote-gated pricing
limitations.explanation: None of the three plans publishes a seat price, and the most valuable features are separately priced add-ons. Total cost cannot be estimated without engaging sales.
limitations.whoItAffects: Buyers running a structured shortlist on published pricing

limitations.title: Telephony operations overhead
limitations.explanation: Number health, carrier reputation, and DNC compliance require ongoing attention that a data or email tool does not. Budget an admin owner, not just seats.
limitations.whoItAffects: Small teams without a RevOps or sales-ops function

deepReview.keyTakeaway: Kixie is the calling layer beneath a sales intelligence stack, not a member of it — buy it for CRM-native dial throughput and conversation coaching, and buy your prospect data somewhere else.
whyWeLike: Automatic CRM activity logging solves a data-completeness problem most teams never fully fix
Conversation Intelligence turns calls into coachable evidence rather than untracked activity
The plan ladder maps to dial volume rather than to arbitrary feature gating
